newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Pacific airlines freight factor unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Asian Pacific airlines freight factor unchanged.

text.p: The freight load factor (FLF) for members of the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines was unchanged for 1996 but the grouping of all major Asian airlines recorded a rise of 1.3 points to 71.4 percent in its passenger load factor (PFL) last year, the AAPA said.

Freight Tonne Kilometres (FTKs) grew in line with freight capacity FATKs leaving Freight Load Factor for the year unchanged at 65.8 percent. FATK's of 39.7 billion outpaced FTKs of 26.1 billion, the statistics show.

AAPA (formerly the Orient Airlines Association) members carried 80.7 million passengers during 1996, a 12.6 percent year on year rise which combined with a 12.5 percent increase in available seat kilometres (ASKs) to 480 billion resulting in the PLF rise.

Statistics for December show Revenue Passenger Kilometres (RPKs) increased 15.1 percent and there was a 14.3 percent rise in the amount of passengers carried. With seat capacity (ASKs) growing at the slower rate of 13.1 percent, Passenger Load Factor (PLF) rose 1.3 percentage points to 71.4 percent during the month.
